members.rationale: EO 3232 amends EO 1888 (1914-02-02) paragraphs 6 and 20, effective 1920-02-20. Paragraph 6 is recurring citizenship/preference, alien-exception and emergency-replacement law; paragraph 20 grants leave privileges. Held EO 4721 I-II creates a limited 100-employee pay exception with restricted leave; EO 8986 sections 1-3 expands to 200, amends paragraphs 6/20 and revokes 4721 and the Secretary of War 1929-08-07 order; EO 9039 authorizes sick/rest leave for otherwise excluded aliens and revokes EO 2993, not EO 3232; EO 9164 revises 8986 section 1, with its own wartime/six-month provision; EO 9467 sections 1 and 4 restate parent paragraphs 6/20, and section 7 revokes 8986/9164. Under strike-and-insert ruling, these amendments are later events, not automatic cessation of the parent provisions. Parent ending and savings remain unproved. Actor text reads are research leads because raw custody/pages are not verified.
members.earlier: Read all five carried actor texts, including their specific exceptions, amendments, revocations and conditional wartime scope. The emergency-replacement condition is an individual application of a recurring rule, not a whole-order sunset. Neither the 1944 threshold rewrite nor 1979 territorial change proves first whole-order cessation. Need EO 1888 original, full subsequent parent history, statutory authority and savings. members.rationale: EO 3973 restates Consular Regulations paragraph 506-1/2 (visually read) as recurring additional-compensation law. Separate rules cover regular/subordinate vice consuls, vacant posts, changes of principal officer, honorary vice consuls, death of the principal and the 50-percent ceiling. The until-new-principal-enters-duty sentence governs an individual salary calculation, not expiration of the regulation. Full held EO 7968 overflow was read (FR pages 1-9): its final Executive Orders Superseded paragraph expressly names EO 3973; V-35 and V-37 supply subsequent compensation rules, V-36 addresses unpaid amounts at death, V-42(b)(3) earned pay and V-56 claims. Thus the machine target-provision-not-located flag is not a legal absence. 1938-09-03 is a candidate supersession date from the held signing date, not an approved first-ending date; original pages, earlier statutory/regulatory history and savings remain open.
